claims.text: In the North Uist lagoon-resident clutches incubated at 14 degrees Celsius, daily observations recorded a visible heartbeat by day 5; by day 7 yolk-sac circulation and developing pectoral fins could be seen. This is an embryo-stage description under the study's incubation conditions, not a diagnostic description of adult morphology.
claims.locator: Results > Development of embryos, days 5 and 7; Figures 3–4; embryos staged from fertilisation at daily intervals.
claims.placeTimeScope: Laboratory observations of embryos from breeding crosses made with North Uist saltwater-lagoon fish collected 30 April–19 May 2023; incubation at 14 degrees Celsius.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild-bred parents; embryos incubated in laboratory dishes.

gaps: Only selected embryonic stages under one temperature and source population are described; adult diagnostic morphology, sexes, age classes, variation across populations, and identification limits remain unassessed.

claims.text: At 14 degrees Celsius, embryos from six migratory and six lagoon-resident North Uist crosses hatched earlier in the migratory ecotype: mean first hatch was 11.7 versus 13.2 days after fertilisation, and mean 50-percent-clutch hatch was 12.2 versus 13.7 days. Hatching success did not differ significantly in this small clutch experiment; these timings do not establish a species-wide rate.
claims.locator: Methods > Fish collection and crosses; Results > Hatching success and time to hatch; Figure 1; Table 1.
claims.placeTimeScope: Crosses using breeding fish collected at Loch an Duin, North Uist, Scotland, 30 April–19 May 2023; embryos raised at 14 degrees Celsius; six clutches per ecotype.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild-bred parents; eggs and embryos were maintained under laboratory conditions.

gaps: The study covers embryonic development to hatching in two local ecotypes only; other life stages, reproduction in natural nests, survival, lifespan, and replication across environments remain unassessed.

claims.text: The study collected breeding migratory and lagoon-resident three-spined stickleback from the same North Uist saltwater lagoon, Loch an Duin, during the 2023 breeding season, and established separate crosses for each ecotype. This establishes local co-occurrence at the collection site and period only; it is not a distribution estimate.
claims.locator: Methods > Fish collection and crosses; Abstract, description of two sympatric saltwater ecotypes.
claims.placeTimeScope: Loch an Duin, a saltwater lagoon in northeast North Uist, Scotland; fieldwork 30 April–19 May 2023.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild breeding adults were caught for crosses; embryos were subsequently incubated in laboratory dishes.

gaps: One breeding-season collection does not describe habitat breadth, diet, species interactions, migration routes, or other populations.
No species-specific phylogenetic or comparative evolutionary analysis was assessed.
The collection site is not a global or range-wide distribution assessment.
No fossil evidence or bounded fossil-record search was assessed.
No current assessment, population trend, or threat analysis was reviewed.

reasons: One primary study supports only selected embryonic, hatching, and collection-site facts.
Four facets remain not assessed; results are limited to two local ecotypes and a laboratory temperature.
No multi-source species review or independent external expert review has been completed.

claims.text: In the author's Skåne monitoring series, start of breeding among local Rana temporaria populations varied by as much as three weeks within a year. The observations span 1990–2015, with the number of monitored ponds varying from 29 to 84 and the most distant ponds separated by 60 kilometres; this is a local monitoring series, not a species-wide phenology estimate.
claims.placeTimeScope: Skåne province, southern Sweden; monitoring from 1990 through 2015; 29–84 ponds depending on year, maximum pond separation 60 km.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild breeding populations observed through their spawn at ponds.

gaps: This local time series does not cover the species' range, other life stages, survival, or reproduction outside the monitored ponds and years.

claims.text: For 19 Skåne ponds with logger data in 2011–2015, earlier mean breeding time was associated with warmer average logged pond temperatures and larger average breeding congregations, estimated from spawn-clump counts; the reported temperature and congregation terms were statistically significant. Substantial residual pond variation remained, and this observational association does not identify a causal mechanism.
claims.locator: Methods > Temperature measurements in ponds; Results paragraph beginning ‘There were effects of pond temperature’; Figure 5.
claims.placeTimeScope: 19 logger ponds in Skåne, southern Sweden; breeding and temperature subset from 2011–2015. Spawn-clump count was used as the breeding-congregation estimate.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild breeding populations; no captive frogs were studied.

gaps: A local pond association does not establish mechanism, diet, habitat use across the range, or ecological interactions beyond breeding-site temperature and congregation size.
No species-specific phylogenetic or comparative evolutionary analysis was assessed.
The Skåne study area is not a range-wide distribution assessment.
No fossil evidence or bounded fossil-record search was assessed.
No current assessment, population trend, or threat analysis was reviewed.

reasons: One regional monitoring study supports only local spawning phenology and pond-level associations.
Five facets remain not assessed; the study does not provide global or species-wide coverage.
No multi-source species review or independent external expert review has been completed.
